title: SAP Porto 2026: The power of the SAP Community, Moshe Naveh
author: deiamolina
text:
This post is part of my SIT Porto 2026 series. Main post: SIT Porto 2026: A first time, and why I'll be back 
 The power of the SAP Community: Simplified Blogging and Personal Branding in the era of AI , by moshenaveh 
 Moshe Naveh is a Senior Community Manager and Advocate for the SAP Community, and he talked about authenticity in the AI era. Always friendly, with a smile on his face, Moshe showed how to use the community to the members' advantage. 
 Watch the talk: https://www.youtube.com/live/grU_TdxhjNY?t=1860s (starts at 0:31). 
 The DOM 
 The DOM (Document Object Model) is how a browser sees a web page: a tree where every title, paragraph and image is a branch. Here's the tree of this post: 
 <post> 
 ├── 1. Why this topic matters to me (and to everyone) 
 │ └── The importance of a non-technical talk in a technology community event 
 ├── 2. Summary of the talk (and my observations) 
 │ ├── Why blogging can be intimidating 
 │ ├── The influencer fallacy 
 │ ├── Simplified blogging 
 │ └── Special initiatives to follow 
 ├── 3. The most important part 
 ├── 4. A special thanks 
 └── 5. The sovereignty challenge (or António's challenge) 
 1. Why this topic matters to me (and to everyone) 
 This topic speaks to my heart. After 20+ years working with SAP, almost 15 of them at the same company, I had built a personal brand inside the company, and that is also why I wasn't part of the SAP Community before: my bubble was internal. While attending an Women's Leadership program, I noticed that, having a external personal brand and becoming more active in the SAP Community would be great not only for me but also for the company. I would be able to share my knowledge and learn a lot to become a better professional. So I started blogging here and how I was very interested on Moshe's presentation. 
 💡 Tip of the day: keep your presence internal and external even when you are not looking for new opportunities. It's the best way to keep yourself updated! The importance of a non-technical talk in a technology community event 
 This was the only talk focused purely on people and community. Many technical people might think this is not as important, but let me remind you, my friend: you are human, you work for humans, you live with humans and you love humans. We are, and should always be, the center of technology. 
 2. Summary of the talk (and my observations) 
 Moshe talked about how to be a valuable participant in the community and get the best out of it: 
 Explore and follow topics 
 Engage with the content 
 Write your own posts and answer questions 
 And with that, you build your personal brand! Why blogging can be intimidating 
 People are afraid of blogging for many reasons, and it can be intimidating even for me, and I love to write: 
 Thinking you don't know enough to share 
 Fear of writing something sensitive about your company (my rule: only publish public information) 
 Not having visibility 
 Concluding, when there are no interactions, that it wasn't worth it The influencer fallacy 
 I believe I have a lot to put on the table, and the presence to sit at the table. But when I post, I don't get 200 likes, and I won't lie: I felt discouraged. 
 And here is what I call the influencer fallacy. We are used to influencers who are famous, and people will like their posts no matter what they post. I don't post for the likes, and I need to remind myself of that all the time. I post to share knowledge and to make real connections. So please keep that in mind too. Simplified blogging 
 Some people are natural communicators and would talk to a wall if no one else were around (me). Others (my husband) have a lot of internal chats, but why bother making them more public? I promise you, when he talks I realize he has as much to say as I do. Those types usally get married hahaha 
 Everybody has opinions and can help others and enrich the community. EVERYBODY! 
 So, if writing is not natural to you, maybe talking is. Maybe talking out loud when you are alone? Great: Moshe found a way for you to put it out in the world, if you want to. 
 Simplified blogging is: create a template, record yourself with a transcript, create a blog post from it using a prompt, review, validate, remove the robot part of the text, review again, make it authentic, and publish! 
 Moshe gave an example: he records himself while walking and transforms it into blog posts. Honestly, I don't see myself doing it (for a reason you'll find in the sovereignty challenge below). I would rather sit down and write, but that's the beauty of life: one size doesn't fit all, and thank God it doesn't. Can you imagine a world with only one kind of person? Boring! 
 Don't forget to always be transparent when you use AI to help you write, check the content of your blog posts before publishing, be authentic, and remember you own your blogs. It's your reputation we are talking about. 
 Special initiatives to follow 
 Before I gave your the wrong directions, let me confirm with Moshe. I will update this post with the proper links, but the initiaves he mentioned are: 
 Hello SAP Community 
 SAP Community Hobbies series 
 Speaker series 
 3. The most important part 
 We do have AI and all today, but we are beautiful creatures with a head full of imagination. All of us, even if you don't realize it. Blogging is a beautiful way to unlock your creative self, and we need more humans and authenticity around 😉 
 4. A special thanks 
 A special thanks to Moshe, who was so open to talk and to help me unlock my blogging too. Thank you a million! 
 5. The sovereignty challenge (or António's challenge) 
 Remember I said I don't see myself recording my voice? Since I don't know where, when and how my data is processed on AI servers, I'm still a bit reluctant to upload my voice and pictures to it. But hey, I'm the cybersecurity-crazy one who puts tape over the phone camera. And before you think this is unsustainable today (and it is: we have cameras everywhere and microphones in our pockets), I still want the illusion that I can somehow control it. Let me be, please 😂 Or feel free to make jokes about me in the comments, I can handle it. 
 That's my take for my voice and pictures, but I do see huge value in these tools too. Maybe in the future, when regulations and laws protect us. I hope we get there soon 🤞

title: Building an MCP Server on Integration Cell part of SAP Integration Suite : APIs to AI Agents
author: nitesh_agrawal2
text:
Credit : In a series of super blogs, my colleague @Ashutosh_KSingh has explained how to set up Integration Cell, What is API Centric Integration and How to get started with MCP servers on Integration Suite. 
 https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-sap/api-centric-integration-on-sap-integration-suite-part-1-build-and-deploy/ba-p/14438357 
 https://community.sap.com/t5/integration-blog-posts/mcp-servers-on-sap-integration-suite-build-your-first-mcp-server-from-an/ba-p/14441034 
 This Blog post builds on this knowledge and works on a scenario comparing SuccessFactors API Consumption via Application vs Agents, powered by MCP servers on Integration Cell. 

 A New Way to Deliver HR Self-Service 
 It is 9 AM on a Monday. John Smith has just joined ABC Corp and is sitting through onboarding. The HR presenter mentions the Company Car benefit. 
 John wants to know what cars he can choose, which vendors are approved, what the lease rates look like, and whether he is already enrolled. The presenter points him to the employee portal. 
 John opens the portal. It does exactly what it was built to do — he finds a Car Options screen with approved models, vendors, and lease providers, and a second screen showing his enrollment status. The portal works well for the questions it was designed to answer. 
 Then John asks a follow-up: "Which provider gives me the best deal for a Toyota?" That one is not on any screen. He opens a helpdesk ticket and gets a reply two days later. 
 This is a familiar and reasonable situation. HR portals are purpose-built, well-governed, and take significant effort to deliver — typically 8 to 12 weeks. They serve the majority of employee needs well. The challenge is the long tail: every new question that was not anticipated at design time either goes unanswered or triggers a new development sprint. 
 This blog introduces a complementary approach — using Integration Cell, part of SAP Integration Suite's MCP capability to expose the same SuccessFactors APIs as AI agent tools, so that employees can ask questions in natural language and get answers beyond what any fixed screen provides. 

 Part 1: The Data Model — SuccessFactors Company Car APIs 
 Before building anything, it helps to understand what APIs we are working with. 
 SAP SuccessFactors exposes its benefits domain via OData v2. The Company Car benefit has six entities, arranged in three clean layers. 
 The Three Layers 
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Layer 1 — Reference Data │
│ ┌──────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────┐ │
│ │ AllowedModels │ │ RecommendedVendors │ │
│ │ Toyota, Nissan, VW │ │ Hertz, AVIS │ │
│ └──────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────┘ │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ LeaseServiceProvider │ │
│ │ AVIS Rental (10.20%), LeasePlan │ │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────┘ │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 2 — Policy │
│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ BenefitCompanyCar │ │
│ │ Lock-in period, maintenance, buyback, EMI freq │ │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 3 — Employee Transactions │
│ ┌──────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────┐ │
│ │ CompanyCarEnrollment │ │ CompanyCarClaim │ │
│ │ John's enrollment │ │ John's claims │ │
│ └──────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 
 The full API spec is available on SAP API Business Accelerator Hub : https://hub.sap.com/api/ECGlobalBenefits/overview 

 Part 2: Building the MCP Server on SAP Integration Suite 
 SAP Integration Suite's Integration Cell runtime supports creating MCP servers directly from an OpenAPI specification — no custom code required. Here is how to set it up, step by step. 
 Step 1 — Get the OpenAPI Spec 
 Download the API spec from SAP API Business Accelerator Hub (search for "Global Benefits" ). The spec is in OpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger) format. 
 Important: Integration Suite's MCP server requires OpenAPI 3.0 . Use any AI tool (or the Swagger Converter) to upgrade the spec from 2.0 to 3.0 before proceeding. 

 Step 2 — Create an Integration Package 
 Log in to your Integration Suite tenant and navigate to Design → Integration Packages . Create a new integration package to hold your MCP server artifact. 
 Step 3 — Add an MCP Server Artifact 
 Inside the package, click Add → MCP Server . 

 In the creation wizard: 
 Select HTTP Endpoint with OpenAPI Specification as the connection type 
 Set Method to Upload 
 Upload your OpenAPI 3.0 spec file 
 Set the virtual host path — for example: <Virtual Host>/sfsf 

 This is where your MCP endpoint URL will be hosted. 
 Step 4 — Select Your Tools 
 After uploading the spec, the wizard discovers all available API paths as potential tools. Search for "Company Car" in the search field and select all 12 related tools. Click Add . 

 The MCP server artifact is now created. 

 Step 5 — Configure Tools, Prompts, and Resources 
 Open the MCP server artifact and switch to the MCP Configuration tab. You will see four sections: Source | Tools | Resources | Prompts . 

 Under Tools , you can: 
 View all selected tools 
 Add or remove tools 
 Click any tool to inspect its Input Schema and Output Schema 
 Edit tool names and descriptions in edit mode 
 Pro tip: Invest time in editing tool descriptions. The natural language description you write for each tool is what the AI agent reads when deciding which tools to call. A clear description like "Returns the list of car models the company has approved for the benefit program" is far more useful to an agent than "BenefitCompanyCarAllowedModels" . 
 Similarly, the Prompts and Resources sections can be enriched with additional context per the MCP specification. 
 Step 6 — Configure Policies 
 Click the Policies section to view what is applied to the MCP endpoint. 

 Authentication and Authorization are applied by default. 
 In the Authentication policy settings, add Basic authentication — this supports Process Integration Runtime (PIR) credentials, which is how agents will authenticate when calling the MCP server. OAuth (client credentials) and Client Certificate authentication are also supported. 

 For Authorization , keep the default settings. The scope API.invoke is required — the JWT token issued using PIR credentials already contains this scope. 

 Other policies — traffic management, IP filter — are available from the policy palette. We will cover these in a later article in this series. 

 Step 7 — Configure the Backend Connection 
 Before deploying, configure authentication for the SuccessFactors target endpoint. 
 Click on the HTTP receiver adapter and: 
 Set Authentication to Basic 
 Enter the Credential Name — for example, sfsf (a credential stored in the Security Material section of Integration Suite, containing your SuccessFactors username and password) 

 Step 8 — Deploy 
 Save the artifact and click Deploy . Select Integration Cell as the Runtime Profile. The virtual host will be pre-populated. 

 Once deployed, the artifact status changes to Deployed . 

 Step 9 — Grab the MCP Endpoint URL 
 Navigate to Monitor → Integrations and APIs , set Runtime to Integration Cell , and click the Manage Integration Content tile → Started . 
 Your MCP Server artifact appears at the top. The endpoint URL is visible in the right panel — this is the URL you will configure in any AI agent. 

 Part 3: Connecting an AI Agent 
 The MCP endpoint can be connected to any MCP-compatible AI client — Joule (SAP's own AI assistant), Claude Desktop, Cline, GitHub Copilot, and others. 
 Getting Credentials 
 The agent authenticates using Process Integration Runtime (PIR) service key credentials. These are the same credentials used to invoke Integration Flows — retrieve them from the service key of your PIR instance on SAP BTP. 

 Connecting Joule 
 In this demo we use Joule Work Desktop — SAP's generative AI assistant and agent orchestrator. Joule supports external MCP server connections. 

 Once connected, Joule discovers all 12 tools exposed by the MCP server automatically. No further configuration is needed — the agent is ready to reason. 

 Connecting Claude / Cline 
 For Claude Desktop or Cline, the MCP configuration looks like this: 
 { 
 "mcpServers" : { 
 "sfsf-company-car" : { 
 "type" : "http" , 
 "url" : "https://<virtual-host>/sfsf" , 
 "headers" : { 
 "Authorization" : "Basic <base64-encoded-pir-credentials>" 
 } 
 } 
 } 
 } 

 Part 4: The Experience — John Meets His AI Agent 
 ABC Corp has deployed the MCP server. John opens his AI assistant and types his questions exactly as he would ask a colleague. 
 Question 1 — "What are my car options?" 
 "I'm an employee looking to enroll in the company car benefit. What car models can I choose from, which vendors are recommended, and what lease service providers are available?" 
 The agent reasons silently and calls three tools in parallel: get_allowed_car_models , get_recommended_vendors , get_lease_providers . 
 Agent responds — 
 Hi John! Here's what your company car benefit offers: 
 Approved Models: Toyota, Nissan, Volkswagen 
 Approved Vendors: Hertz, AVIS 
 Lease Financing: Provider Monthly EMI Rate 
 AVIS Rental 10.20% 
 LeasePlan Contact HR for rate 
 Installments are paid monthly. Let me know if you'd like details on policy terms! 

 We can see the conversation with Joule and the tool calls it made on the right side. 

 Question 2 — "What is my enrollment and claim status?" 
 "Can you show me the current company car benefit policies, my enrollment details, and whether I have any open claims?" 
 The agent calls get_car_benefit_policy , get_employee_car_enrollment , and get_employee_car_claims in parallel. 
 Agent responds: 
 Policy: Three active car benefit policies, all with monthly installment frequency. 
 Your Enrollment: You have an active enrollment (ID: 163585), but it is incomplete — your car model, vendor, and EMI amount have not been selected yet. 
 Claims: No claims on file. 
 Next step: Complete your enrollment by selecting a model and a financing option. Want help comparing them? 

 The Follow-up — Where the Agent Extends Beyond the Portal 
 "Which lease provider gives me the best deal if I go with a Toyota?" 
 This question sits outside what the portal was designed to show — it would normally mean a helpdesk ticket and a future sprint. 
 With the MCP agent, no new development is needed. The agent re-reads the lease provider and policy data already retrieved: 
 The only provider currently showing a configured EMI rate is AVIS Rental at 10.20% — LeasePlan's rate is not yet set in the system. For a Toyota, AVIS Rental is your best available option. I'd recommend confirming the exact monthly EMI with HR, since it depends on the car's purchase value. 

 Zero development. Zero tickets. Answered in seconds. 

 Part 5: Portal and Agent — Better Together 
 The portal and the MCP agent are not competing approaches — they serve different needs. The portal delivers a reliable, governed, designed experience for the majority of employee interactions. The agent handles the long tail: the follow-up question, the cross-entity comparison, the query no one thought to build a screen for. 
 Architecture Comparison 
 HR Portal: 
 John opens the portal
 │
 ▼
IT-built portal backend
 ├── API call 1 → AllowedModels
 ├── API call 2 → RecommendedVendors
 ├── API call 3 → LeaseServiceProvider
 ├── API call 4 → BenefitCompanyCar
 ├── API call 5 → CompanyCarEnrollment
 └── API call 6 → CompanyCarClaim
 │
 ▼
 JOIN logic in backend
 │
 ▼
 Designed screen renders the data
 │
 ▼
 John gets a reliable, consistent answer
 for questions the portal was built to answer 
 MCP Agent: 
 John's natural language question
 │
 ▼
AI Agent (Joule / Claude / Cline)
 │
 ▼
MCP Server on SAP Integration Suite
 ├── get_allowed_car_models ──→ SF OData

title: Releasing SAC Pilot: The Ultimate Productivity Browser Extension for SAP Analytics Cloud
author: rohitchouhan
text:
If you build stories, write analytical scripts, configure planning simulations, or manage models inside SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), you know the daily friction all too well: 
 You are deep in the middle of designing a critical dashboard or calculation, and you need to look up a specific Cost Center code, Hierarchy parent node, or Dimension Member ID. 
 You have to navigate completely away from your active story canvas or launch an entirely separate browser tab. 
 The SAC Modeler takes 30 to 60 seconds to boot up its heavy menus, breaking your concentration and flow. 
 You only wanted a quick master data export or a clean CSV extract of fact data, but you were forced to step through a multi-step export wizard. 
 Transporting stories between Development, QA, and Production environments often breaks unexpectedly because a single dimension member was missing or had different attributes across tenants. 
 We built SAC Pilot to eliminate this friction once and for all. It is an independent, 100% client-side browser extension that sits pinned right inside your browser's native side panel, auto-detects your active SAP Analytics Cloud session, and helps you work faster without ever leaving your canvas. 
 What is SAC Pilot? 

 SAC Pilot is an open-community, high-performance browser extension crafted specifically for SAC Story Designers, Planners, BI Consultants, and Enterprise Architects. It operates directly alongside your active SAP Analytics Cloud workspace across Google Chrome (recommended), Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, and Mozilla Firefox . 
 Unlike traditional add-ons or middleware that require server installations, database connections, or complicated OAuth setup, SAC Pilot uses a Zero-Configuration, Zero-Trust architecture. It securely senses your existing, authenticated browser session cookie and directly queries the tenant's REST and OData APIs over HTTPS. 
 Key Features & Capabilities 
 SAC Pilot packs over 15+ specialized power tools and utilities into a single, cohesive side-panel interface: 
 1. Instant Model & Data Provider Browser 
 Features type-ahead autocomplete search across all Analytical Models, Planning Models, and Data Providers configured within your tenant. You can view technical model IDs, descriptions, and data source metadata instantly, and switch between models in a single click without page reloads. 
 2. Dimension Member & Hierarchy Tree Explorer 
 Look up dimension member IDs, descriptions, and custom property attributes in sub-seconds. Explore complex parent-child hierarchy trees with interactive rollup expansion, allowing you to trace drill-down levels and aggregation paths on the fly. 
 3. High-Throughput Fact Data Exporter 
 Stream millions of transactional fact records directly from SAC models at blazing speeds (up to 100,000+ records per second) with live throughput progress indicators and time-remaining estimates. Download pristine CSV or JSON extracts ready for Microsoft Excel, Python, or data pipelines. 
 4. Reverse CSV Fact Data Importer 
 Upload external CSV datasets directly back into your SAC planning models without opening backend data integration wizards. The tool maps columns, validates schemas, and pushes records directly into the model. 
 5. Visual Column & Measure Filter Builder 
 Construct complex OData query filters visually before downloading data. Filter by dimension members, posting periods, version tags, or numerical measure ranges to retrieve only the exact dataset slice you need. 
 6. Planning Version Manager (Edit, Copy & Publish) 
 Inspect both Public and Private planning versions at a glance. Review version publication states, ownership, and creation timestamps. Trigger one-click data publishing, create version copies, and manage planning simulations effortlessly. 
 7. User & Team Inspector (SCIM Governance) 
 Audit and search tenant users, email directories, assigned roles, and security teams without needing full SAC Administration menu access. Perfect for validating permissions and verifying user provisioning. 
 8. Currency Exchange Rate Inspector 
 Instantly inspect Currency Conversion Tables configured on your tenant. Review exchange rate types, source and target currency pairs, and effective date validity ranges without opening Modeler settings. 
 9. Multi-Tenant Comparator (Dev vs. QA vs. Prod) 
 Compare dimension structures and member records between two different SAC tenant environments. The diff engine flags synced members, attribute differences, and missing members in the target tenant, helping you catch missing master data before transporting stories. 
 10. Synthetic Mock Test Data Generator 
 Automatically generate structured, realistic mock transactional fact data matching your model's exact dimension schemas. Configure cardinality, random distributions, and date ranges to stage models for testing and demonstration. 
 11. In-Panel Visualizer & Analytics 
 Embedded Chart.js analytics right inside the extension panel. Render instant bar charts, measure distribution curves, and member cardinality breakdowns without needing to create disposable story widgets. 
 12. Smart Bookmarks & Saved Filter Queries 
 Bookmark your most frequently accessed models, dimensions, and custom filter configurations. Jump straight into your daily operational views with one click. 
 13. 1-Click Clipboard Utilities 
 Copy individual member IDs, formatted string arrays, or JSON arrays directly to your system clipboard, formatted specifically for pasting into SAC story calculation scripts, advanced formulas, or SQL queries. 
 14. Public Dimensions Explorer 
 Dedicated inspection view for tenant-wide shared Public Dimensions, allowing you to audit global master data independent of individual analytical models. 
 15. Application Audit Logs Explorer 
 Inspect model application audit logs and change histories directly within the extension to audit updates and track modifications. 
 16. Deep Link Story & Modeler Navigator 
 Generate one-click direct deep links to navigate straight to the exact model or story in the native SAC interface. 
 Feature Overview Table 

 Feature Category Tool Name Primary Benefits Target User 
 Data Export High-Throughput Fact Exporter Stream fact data at 100k+ rows/sec to CSV/JSON BI Analysts & Data Engineers 
 Data Import Reverse CSV Importer Push external fact datasets into models Planners & Data Modelers 
 Master Data Dimension & Hierarchy Explorer Instant member search & parent-child tree drill-down Story Designers & Planners 
 Planning Version Manager Review, copy, and publish planning versions in 1 click Financial Planners 
 Governance User & Team Inspector SCIM audit of users, roles, and teams Administrators & Leads 
 Quality Assurance Tenant Comparator Diff dimensions across Dev, QA, and Prod Release Managers & Architects 
 Testing Test Data Generator Generate synthetic mock facts based on model schema Model Developers & Testers 
 Finance Currency Table Inspector Audit conversion rates and currency pairs Financial Controllers 
 Productivity Smart Bookmarks & Clipboard Save frequent queries and copy arrays for scripting All SAC Users 
 Security AES-256 GCM Storage Vault Zero-trust, client-side encryption of all local caches Security & Compliance Teams 
 Zero-Trust Architecture & Enterprise Security 
 Enterprise data privacy is non-negotiable. SAC Pilot was designed from the ground up to comply with strict enterprise IT security standards: 
 100% Client-Side Operation: The extension operates entirely within your local browser. There are no intermediate proxy servers, cloud relays, or backend databases. 
 Direct HTTPS Communication: Every network call is dispatched directly between your browser and your authenticated SAC tenant domain. 
 No Telemetry or Tracking: SAC Pilot collects zero personal information, logs no tenant activity, and includes no third-party tracking scripts. 
 AES-256 GCM Encrypted Vault: Any data persisted locally (such as bookmarks and cached dimension names) is encrypted using the browser's native Web Crypto API before being written to storage. 
 Session Cookie Inheritance: SAC Pilot never asks for, stores, or handles your password. It relies entirely on your browser's existing authenticated SAC session cookie. 
 Instant Data Purge: A dedicated single-click "Wipe Storage" option in the Settings panel allows you to instantly purge all stored keys, bookmarks, and local data. 
 How to Install & Get Started 
 You can install SAC Pilot directly from the official portal: 
 Official Installation Website: sac-pilot.rohitchouhan.com 
 Easy 3-Step Installation: 
 Go to sac-pilot.rohitchouhan.com in your browser. 
 Click the install button for your browser (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, or Mozilla Firefox). 
 Confirm the prompt to add the extension to your browser. 
 Getting Started in 60 Seconds: 
 Log in to your regular SAP Analytics Cloud tenant. 
 Open SAC Pilot by clicking the extension icon in your browser toolbar or opening your browser's native Side Panel. 
 The extension automatically detects your active authenticated SAC session — no API keys, logins, or configurations needed. 
 Select any tool from the Home screen (such as Data Export/Import , Dimension Explorer , or Version Manager ) and start exploring your data right beside your active stories. 
 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) 
 Does SAC Pilot require an API key, Login Credentials or SAC OAuth client setup? 
 No. SAC Pilot automatically uses your existing authenticated browser session cookies to interact with SAC's standard endpoints. No administrator API configuration is required. 
 Can SAC Pilot see or transmit my company's data? 
 Never. SAC Pilot runs 100% inside your client browser. It never connects to any external third-party server. All data stays strictly between your browser and your company's official SAC tenant. 
 Does it support both Classic and New Planning Models? 
 Yes. SAC Pilot supports Analytical Models, Classic Account Models, and the New Model (Measure-based) type. 
 Is SAC Pilot free to use? 
 Yes, SAC Pilot is an open-community tool designed to give back to the SAP Analytics Cloud ecosystem. 
 Legal Disclaimer & Trademark Notice 
 Please review the following legal disclosures regarding SAC Pilot: 
 Not an Official SAP Extension: SAC Pilot is an independent third-party project created by Rohit Chouhan. It is not developed, tested, certified, maintained, supported, or endorsed by SAP SE. 
 Trademark Ownership: SAP, SAP Analytics Cloud, SAP HANA, SAP BTP, and other SAP products and services mentioned herein, as well as their respective logos, are trademarks or registered trademarks of SAP SE in Germany and other countries worldwide. All other company, product, and service names used are for identification purposes only and belong to their respective owners. 
 Independent Companion Tool: This tool is created independently as an open-community utility for SAP Analytics Cloud practitioners to improve productivity. 
 No Official Affiliation: Reference to SAP Analytics Cloud does not imply any affiliation with or endorsement by SAP SE. The official SAP website is located at https://www.sap.com . 
 Warranty & Compliance: This software is provided on an "as-is" basis without warranties of any kind. Users are responsible for adhering to their organization's internal data governance and security policies when handling corporate tenant data. 
 Conclusion 
 SAC Pilot transforms the way professionals interact with SAP Analytics Cloud by removing friction, accelerating daily tasks, and providing deep data visibility right beside your active work. Whether you are validating a single dimension member, streaming a million fact records, or diffing master data across enterprise environments, SAC Pilot is your trusted companion.

title: Cross-border data transfer questions for CPQ - CPQ DC in Frankfurt while S4 are hosted in China
author: JuliaLu
text:
Our China CRM and SAP S/4HANA are hosted in mainland China, while SAP CPQ will be hosted overseas in Frankfurt, German, due to CPQ has no data center in mainland China. Seek security expert guidance for below questions. Thank you very much. 
 1) Is any personally identifiable information (PII) processed within SAP CPQ that would be stored or transferred outside of China? 
 2) What performance implications should we expect when SAP CPQ traffic must pass through the Chinese firewall? 
 3) Are there any architectural or technical options available to mitigate potential latency or compliance concerns?
